preamble: Nasalization of [i] to [ĩ] arises when the vowel absorbs a following nasal consonant. In Portuguese, Latin -īn- in word-final position yielded a nasal vowel (Latin fīnem > fim [ˈfĩ] 'end'), and in Hindi a vowel before a nasal + stop cluster became a long nasal vowel when the nasal was lost (Sanskrit siñcati > Hindi sī̃cnā 'to irrigate').

examples.note: Via Old Galician-Portuguese fim/fin; the coda nasal was absorbed into the vowel, which surfaces as [ĩ] in both Brazilian and European Portuguese.
Inherited via Prakrit and Apabhramsa; the nasal of the -ñc- cluster was lost and the preceding vowel became long and nasalized.

sources: Masica, C. P. (1991). The Indo-Aryan Languages. Cambridge University Press.
